function: AirComp FL model aggregation at an ISAC base station: transmit and receive beamforming plus device selection minimizing the FL convergence-bound error under a radar-SNR constraint (pp. 1, 8-11).
system: BS with 32 transmit and 32 receive ULA antennas, 30 single-antenna devices, one radar target, analog downlink and AirComp uplink, no RIS, band unstated (pp. 3, 11).
method: Federated learning of a CNN with AirComp aggregation; beamforming and device selection come from SDR, SCA and greedy device elimination, not learned (pp. 3, 9-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d) with Rayleigh small-scale fading, devices randomly placed 10-200 m from BS; MNIST and Fashion-MNIST for the FL task (p. 11).
test_conditions: Separate FL runs per scheme and BS antenna count (16 to 128) on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST test sets; no unseen channel or configuration test (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Ideal error-free FL [4], without device selection, random device selection [40], random beamforming, downlink-free, single receive beamformer without the proposed approach [41], [42] (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Test accuracy versus FL iteration round on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST (Figs. 2-4); no sensing metric reported, radar SNR only as constraint (pp. 11-13).
q1_support: p. 11: "The small-scale fading follows Rayleigh fading"; the path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d) cites 3GPP TR 36.819 [38] (p. 16), a path-loss formula only. Missing: no 3GPP TR 38.901 or 38.811, DeepMIMO, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100 or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 13: "Here, the transceiver beamforming vectors are optimized using the proposed Algorithms 1 and 2" for each antenna count of Fig. 4. Missing: no model trained in one configuration and tested in another, each scheme or antenna count is a separate FL run.
q3_support: p. 12: "Based on the randomly selected device set, the transceiver beamforming vectors are optimized using Algorithms 1 and 2"; p. 12: "only a single receive beamforming vector is used by the BS". Missing: no baseline is stated to be an earlier published aggregation design, they are own heuristics or ablations.
q4_support: p. 11: "we consider to train a convolution neural network (CNN)" is the only cost-related description, the size of the FL model. Missing: no complexity order, operation count, parameter count or runtime of the transceiver design.
q5_support: p. 11: "MNIST and fashion-MNIST data sets to validate the performance of the proposed algorithm in practical FL tasks"; learning-task data sets only, channels simulated, no code or data link.
notes: Included as area 7: the learned element is the FL model trained over the air and the paper solves its AirComp aggregation under a sensing constraint, so 7 wins over 5 (ISAC). The transceiver design is classical optimization, accepted under the FL-over-the-air rule. q3 borderline: the closest published design, a single receive beamformer cited to [41], [42], is defined as the method without its receive-beamforming module.
